'''Idelisa Bonnelly de Calventi''' (10 September 1931 – 3 July 2022)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=3 July 2022 |title=Muere Idelisa Bonnelly de Calventi, madre de la conservación marina |url=https://listindiario.com/la-vida/2022/07/03/728581/muere-idelisa-bonnelly-de-calventi-madre-de-la-conservacion-marina |access-date=5 July 2022 |website=listindiario.com |language=es-DO |archive-date=4 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704184106/https://listindiario.com/la-vida/2022/07/03/728581/muere-idelisa-bonnelly-de-calventi-madre-de-la-conservacion-marina |url-status=live }}</ref> was a [[Dominican Republic|Dominican]] [[marine biologist]] who is considered the "mother of [[marine conservation]] in the [[Caribbean]]".<ref name=mom>{{cite news|title=Ecuatoriana entre las 10 científicas más destacadas de Latinoamérica|url=http://www.eluniverso.com/vida-estilo/2013/10/18/nota/1598816/ecuatoriana-10-cientificas-mas-destacadas-latinoamerica|access-date=12 November 2015|publisher=El Universo|date=18 October 2013|location=Alban, Guayaquil, Ecuador|language=es|archive-date=27 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327124719/https://www.eluniverso.com/vida-estilo/2013/10/18/nota/1598816/ecuatoriana-10-cientificas-mas-destacadas-latinoamerica|url-status=live}}</ref> She was the founder of the study of biology in the Dominican Republic, as well as the founder of the Institute of Marine Biology and the Dominican Foundation for Marine Research. She was instrumental in the creation of the first Humpback Whale Sanctuary of the North Atlantic and has won numerous awards, including induction into the UNEP's [[Global 500 Roll of Honour]], UNESCO's Marie Curie Medal and the [[Order of Merit of Duarte, Sánchez and Mella]]. The BBC has called her one of the most important women scientists in Latin America.

==Biography==
Idelisa Bonnelly Peralta was born on 10 September 1931 in [[Santiago de los Caballeros]], Dominican Republic.<ref name=bio>{{cite news|title=Reconocen trayectoria de la maestra Idelisa Bonnelly|url=http://www.intec.edu.do/noticias-y-actividades/noticias/item/reconocen-trayectoria-de-la-maestra-idelisa-bonnelly|access-date=12 November 2015|publisher=Instituto Tecnológico de Santo Domingo|date=19 November 2014|location=Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic|language=es|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043512/http://www.intec.edu.do/noticias-y-actividades/noticias/item/reconocen-trayectoria-de-la-maestra-idelisa-bonnelly|url-status=live}}</ref> As she wanted to study marine biology and there were no schools teaching biology in the Dominican Republic, she pursued her university studies in New York.<ref name="Life Magazine"/> In 1953, she enrolled at [[Columbia University]], graduating with a BS in marine biology in 1956. She went on to attain a master's degree from [[New York University]] in 1961.<ref name=bio /> After completion of her schooling, Bonnelly began her first job at the [[New York Aquarium]] as a research assistant to Ross Nigrelli.{{Who|date=October 2022}}<ref name=bio />

In 1962, she returned to the Dominican Republic and began teaching at the [[Universidad Autónoma de Santo Domingo]] (UASD), founding the first institution for the study of biology in the country. In 1966, she founded the Institute of Marine Biology, which later became the Research Center of Marine Biology ({{langx|es|Centro de Investigación de Biología Marina}}),<ref name="Life Magazine">{{cite news|last1=Álvarez|first1=Venecia|title=Reconocimiento a la Sra. Idelissa Bonelly|url=http://www.revistavitard.com/articulos/familia/53-reconocimiento-a-la-sra-idelissa-bonelly.html|access-date=12 November 2015|publisher=Revista Vita República Dominicana|date=6 April 2010|location=Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117015031/http://www.revistavitard.com/articulos/familia/53-reconocimiento-a-la-sra-idelissa-bonelly.html|archive-date=17 November 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> at which she taught from 1967 to 1986 and then until 1992 served as the coordinator of graduate studies.<ref name=bio />

In 1974, Bonnelly founded the Academy of Sciences of the Dominican Republic<ref name=IANAS>{{cite web|title=Idelisa Bonnelly – República Dominicana|url=http://www.ianas.org/women_bio_bonnelly.html|publisher=Interamerican Network of Academies of Sciences|access-date=12 November 2015|location=Mexico City, Mexico|language=es|date=2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117023258/http://www.ianas.org/women_bio_bonnelly.html|archive-date=17 November 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> and began publishing works which became widely influential for those managing and concerned with conservation of marine resources. In 1986, she was instrumental in the creation of the first protected area for the [[humpback whale]], originally called the Humpback Whale Sanctuary on the Silver Bank ({{langx|es|Santuario de Ballenas Jorobadas del Banco de la Plata}}) but today known as {{Interlanguage link|Santuario de los Bancos de la Plata y la Navidad|es}}.<ref name=bio /> For her contributions, she was awarded the Medal of Merit of Dominican Women in Science by the Government of the Dominican Republic (1986), the National Science Prize from the Academy of Sciences of the Dominican Republic (1987), and was inducted into the [[Global 500 Roll of Honour]] by the [[United Nations Environment Programme]] (UNEP) in 1987.<ref name="Life Magazine" /><ref name=IANAS />

She became a Professor Meritorious at (UASD) in 1990 and in 1991 she created the Dominican Foundation for Marine Research ({{langx|es|Fundación Dominicana de Estudios Marinos}}) (FUNDEMAR), an institution which coordinates the marine management plan, studies marine life and the coral reef, and manages the Marine Mammal Sanctuary.<ref name=bio /> That same year, Bonnelly joined the [[Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World]] (OWSD) and served in the First General Assembly.<ref name=IANAS /> She continued publishing and her works have been utilized for influencing marine and coastal [[Environmental Law]].<ref name=bio /> Bonnelly was made an academic laureate of the Academy of Sciences in 2007, received a National Ecology Award from the [[Grupo Corripio|Fundación Corripio]] in 2008, and was awarded the [[Marie Curie]] Medal from UNESCO in 2009.<ref name=IANAS />

In 2010, the Society for the Conservation of Biology of [[Victoria, British Columbia]], Canada, honored her with a Distinguished Service Award in Biology and in 2011, the Government of the Dominican Republic granted her the [[Order of Merit of Duarte, Sánchez and Mella]].<ref name=bio /> In 2013, she was recognized by the BBC as one of the ten most important women scientists in [[Latin America]].<ref name=mom />

==Death==
Idelisa Bonnelly died on 3 July 2022 at the age of 90.{{Where|date=October 2022}}<ref name=":0" />

== Awards ==
* 1986 Medal of Merit for Women in Science, Government of the Dominican Republic<ref name="Life Magazine" />
* 1987 National Science Prize, Academy of Sciences of the Dominican Republic<ref name="Life Magazine" />
* 1987 Global 500 Roll of Honour, United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)<ref name="Life Magazine" />
* 1990 Meritorious professor Autonomous University of Santo Domingo<ref name="Life Magazine" />
* 2007 Academic Laureate Academy of Sciences of the Dominican Republic<ref name=IANAS />
* 2008 National Ecology Award, [[Grupo Corripio|Fundación Corripio]]<ref name=IANAS />
* 2009 Marie Curie Medal,<ref name=UNESCO>{{cite web|title=Marie Curie|url=http://portal.unesco.org/en/ev.php-URL_ID=26471&URL_DO=DO_TOPIC&URL_SECTION=201.html|publisher=UNESCO|access-date=12 November 2015|archive-date=29 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190329234208/http://portal.unesco.org/en/ev.php-URL_ID%3D26471%26URL_DO%3DDO_TOPIC%26URL_SECTION%3D201.html|url-status=live}}</ref> UNESCO<ref name=IANAS />
* 2010 Distinguished Service Award in Biology (SCB), Society for the Conservation of Biology, Victoria, Canada, 2010<ref name=bio />
* 2011 Order of Merit of Duarte, Sánchez and Mella, Government of the Dominican Republic<ref name=bio />
